requirements.title: CalOPPA: privacy policy conspicuously posted

criteria: Operator of a commercial website or online service that collects personally identifiable information (e.g., name, address, email, phone) from California residents who use or visit it.
business_types: volteira.com (SaaS marketing site, Shadam LLC)
pacificplainselectric.com (California electrical contractor, Pacific Plains Electric)
exceptions: Internet service providers transmitting third-party content are not 'operators' for that activity.

required_behavior: The privacy policy is 'conspicuously posted' by at least one method in B&P 22577(b): (1) the policy itself appears on the homepage; (2) it appears on the first significant page after entering the site; (3) an icon hyperlink to it that contains the word 'privacy' appears on the homepage or first significant page, in a color that contrasts with the page background; (4) a text hyperlink that includes the word 'privacy' appears on the homepage or first significant page, written in capital letters equal to or greater in size than the surrounding text, or in larger type than surrounding text, or in contrasting type, font or color to surrounding text of the same size, or set off by symbols or marks that call attention to it; or (5) any other functional hyperlink so displayed that a reasonable person would notice it.
The link resolves (HTTP 200) to the current policy and is present on every page template (footer) as good practice.
requirements.enforcement_exposure: AG enforcement under UCL (B&P 17200) after 30-day notice to cure (22575(a)); penalties up to $2,500 per violation under UCL.
required_evidence: DOM capture of the link text and href
requirements.notes: Check: find an <a> on the homepage whose text contains 'privacy' (case-insensitive) and verify styling meets one of the (b)(4) options; record which 22577(b) method is satisfied. requirements.title: CCPA: notice at collection at or before collection points

criteria: Applies only to a 'business' under Civ. Code 1798.140(d): for-profit entity doing business in California that collects consumers' personal information and (A) has annual gross revenue above the CPI-adjusted threshold (US$25,000,000 in statute, adjusted by the CPPA; reported as US$26,625,000 from January 1, 2025 — confirm current figure), or (B) annually buys, sells or shares personal information of 100,000 or more California consumers or households, or (C) derives 50% or more of annual revenue from selling or sharing personal information.
Pacific Plains Electric: likely below thresholds unless revenue exceeds the adjusted figure; record the determination.
Shadam LLC (Volteira): a 'business' for its own marketing-site visitors only if a threshold is met; acts as a 'service provider' (1798.140(ag)) for contractor tenants' customer data.
business_types: volteira.com (SaaS marketing site, Shadam LLC)
pacificplainselectric.com (California electrical contractor, Pacific Plains Electric)
exceptions: Not applicable to entities below all thresholds (CalOPPA still applies).
Certain B2B and employee data exemptions expired January 1, 2023; B2B contacts are covered consumers.

required_behavior: At or before each point of collection (quote/booking/contact forms, SMS opt-in, newsletter, chat, cookies), a notice or a conspicuous link to it states: categories of personal information (incl. sensitive) collected, purposes, whether each category is sold or shared, retention period or criteria, and a link to the privacy policy; and, if the business sells/shares, the 'Do Not Sell or Share' link.
For online collection, the link appears on the page where data is collected (e.g., beneath the form submit button) and on the homepage.
required_evidence: screenshots of each form with notice/link

requirements.title: CCPA: opt-out preference signal (GPC) honored

AB 566 (Opt Me Out Act) requires browsers to offer an opt-out preference signal from January 1, 2027.

criteria: Applies only to a 'business' under Civ. required_behavior: A browser sending a Global Privacy Control signal (Sec-GPC: 1 header / navigator.globalPrivacyControl) is treated as a valid request to opt out of sale/sharing for that browser (and any known consumer profile), without requiring further action.

criteria: Site loads third-party code that captures communications or interactions in real time: session replay (e.g., Hotjar, FullStory, Microsoft Clarity, LogRocket), third-party chat/AI chat widgets, form-field keystroke capture, or ad/analytics pixels transmitting URLs/form data to third parties.

requirements.title: Shine the Light: direct-marketing disclosure rights (if applicable)

criteria: Business with an established business relationship that discloses customers' personal information to third parties for their direct marketing purposes.
business_types: volteira.com (SaaS marketing site, Shadam LLC)
pacificplainselectric.com (California electrical contractor, Pacific Plains Electric)
exceptions: Businesses with fewer than 20 full-time or part-time employees are exempt.
May comply via a privacy policy allowing opt-out or opt-in for third-party direct marketing disclosures.

required_behavior: If personal information is disclosed to third parties for their direct marketing, the site provides a designated address/email/toll-free number (or privacy-policy notice) for consumers to request the disclosure information, or offers the opt-out/opt-in alternative.
required_evidence: privacy policy Shine-the-Light section or exemption determination

requirements.title: Bot disclosure for chatbots used to sell

criteria: Site uses an automated chat agent (bot or AI assistant) that communicates with California visitors to incentivize a purchase or sale of goods or services.
business_types: volteira.com (SaaS marketing site, Shadam LLC)
pacificplainselectric.com (California electrical contractor, Pacific Plains Electric)

required_behavior: The chat widget clearly, conspicuously and reasonably discloses that the visitor is communicating with a bot (e.g., 'You're chatting with an AI assistant') so the person is not misled about its artificial identity.
requirements.notes: Liability attaches to use of a bot with intent to mislead about its artificial identity; disclosure provides the statutory safe harbor.
